question: Should OpenClaw add HEARTBEAT.md task-level model metadata, keep heartbeat routing whole-turn via plugins, or design a broader scheduled-task routing contract first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the right API boundary changes public HEARTBEAT.md syntax and model/session routing semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Design scheduled-task routing first
options.body: Create one broader scheduled-task model-routing contract that can cover HEARTBEAT.md tasks and related cron main-session overrides before implementation.

options.title: Add narrow HEARTBEAT.md metadata
options.body: Accept a task-level HEARTBEAT.md model field and implement parser, runner, docs, and tests specifically for heartbeat tasks.

options.title: Keep routing whole-turn via plugins
options.body: Decline per-task heartbeat routing in core and document that existing before_model_resolve hooks only support whole-turn model selection.

recommendation.title: Design scheduled-task routing first
recommendation.body: Create one broader scheduled-task model-routing contract that can cover HEARTBEAT.md tasks and related cron main-session overrides before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He appears in adjacent plugin model-resolution history and is the best available owner for the core-versus-plugin routing boundary decision.
